h: "As If Inside": The Shofar That Reaches the Kodesh HaKodashim

p: that the reason the Sages forbade a cow's horn
is that "an accuser cannot become a defender,"
it is considered as if inside" —
that is, in the Kodesh HaKodashim,
the Kohen Gadol does enter in garments of gold.
"And wisdom — from where, ayin, is it found?":
from the place called Kodesh HaKodashim";
and it explains that the aspect of Ayin
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק ב סד, ב).
and the Kodesh HaKodashim corresponds to Kesser Elyon.
Once I entered to offer the incense, etc.,
and I saw Achtariel Yah, Hashem Tzeva'os,
sitting upon a throne high and exalted."
is the name of Kesser Elyon,
for it contains the letters of "Kesser."
There is also proof from what he said,
"'Your throne is established from then' — az — etc.
The king stands upon the platform
Since You created Your world You are He,
but since You stood at the Sea
and we sang before You with 'Az,'
This is what they said in the holy Zohar
and shines to every side," etc.;
which is the aspect of the revelation of Atika.
Thus, with the revelation of the attribute of Atika,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא אָז ה׳ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא.
so that Hashem is then called "sitting upon a throne."
and the Ancient of Days sat."
And the mitzvah is to hear the sound of the shofar
(רֹאשׁ, רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה פֶּרֶק ד סִימָן י;
for Hashem Yisbarach too is called
"Who hears the sound of the shofar and gives ear to the teruah"
in the text of the Shofaros blessing,
"And you shall walk in His ways";
to hear the sound of the shofar.
And Hashem Yisbarach sits upon the throne
where the attribute of Kesser Elyon is revealed;
and this is what they said in the Gemara cited above:
And as for its saying "since it is for remembrance" —
the intent follows what they said
"Shamor is in the heart and not in any other place" —
the aspect of "the mother of the children";
"remembering is in the male, in the brain," etc.,
"and therefore Zachor is for the male
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
It is along the lines of what they said in the holy Zohar
"Zachor is a place that has no forgetting
and where forgetting has no place";
that is, the aspect of Atika;
in the Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, in the Zichronos blessing,
כִּי אֵין שִׁכְחָה לִפְנֵי כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ,
"For there is no forgetting before Your throne of glory";
that is, "the Ancient of Days sat."
And this is the upper tip of the Yud,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק ג סה, ב);
and the letters Yud-Hei of the Name Havayah
there shines forth from Kesser Elyon into Chochmah.
And this is "Zachor — remembering is in the brain,"
into which there shines from Kesser Elyon
through the crownlet of the upper Yud.
And this is what they said:
"Since it is for remembrance, it is considered as if inside" —
that is, in the innermost Sanctum.
regarding the blood of the bull
that it is permitted for this reason:
"since it has changed, it has changed."
It is difficult: why did it not ask from the shofar,
but the sound of the shofar alone?
And that is a stronger case than the blood of the bull,
where something of the bull's body enters,
whereas here nothing at all enters
of the substance of the bull,
only the sound of the shofar.
But from this it is clear
that the sound of the shofar rises on high
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹמֵעַ מִשָּׁם הַקּוֹל שׁוֹפָר,
and Hashem Yisbarach hears the sound of the shofar from there;
rather, Hashem Yisbarach, as it were,
and as for Yisrael, at the time they blow,
the one blowing with the shofar is then
as if he had entered the Kodesh HaKodashim.
And this is what they said:
"Since it is for remembrance, it is considered as if inside" —
as though the one blowing were standing
and the shofar has not changed at all
מִכְּפִי מַה שֶּׁהָיָה עַל גּוּף הַפָּר,
from how it was on the body of the bull;
and because of this it is well understood
why the Sages forbade a cow's horn.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 26a — "Ulla said: This is the reason of the Rabbis [for disqualifying a cow's horn]: an accuser cannot become a defender." Rashi: like the gold of the Calf, the horn of a cow is an accuser, recalling the Calf. "And Rabbi Yosi will say to you… that applies within [the Holy of Holies], but this shofar is outside."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 121a (Mishpatim) — "It is written, 'And wisdom (chochmah) — from where (me'ayin) shall it be found?' (Iyov 28:12): the Torah came forth from Chochmah, from the place called Kodesh; and Chochmah came forth from the place called Kodesh HaKodashim."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 27 — “In the holy Zohar (II 121a): ‘And wisdom, from where is it found?’ — wisdom comes forth from the place called Kodesh HaKodashim; ‘from where’ (me'ayin) is the hidden Ancient One of all hidden things, who is called Ayin.” Connection: Both bring this Zohar to identify the Kodesh HaKodashim with the hidden source above Chochmah.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, Beshalach 64b — “Rabbi Abba said: What is meant by ‘Is the Lord in our midst, or nothing?’ Were Israel fools who did not know this matter? Had they not seen the Divine Presence before them and the clouds of glory surrounding them? ... Rather, Rabbi Shimon said this: They wished to know the difference between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, who is called Nothing, and Zeir Anpin, who is called the Lord. ... Why, then, were they punished? Because they made a separation and put it to a test. They said: If it is this One, we will ask in one manner; if it is this One, we will ask in another manner. Therefore, immediately, ‘Amalek came.’” The Zohar interprets Israel's question at Massah as a question about the degree from which Divine governance was being revealed. It explicitly names the concealed Atika as Ayin.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 7a — "R. Yishmael ben Elisha said: Once I entered the innermost sanctum to offer incense, and I saw Achtriel Yah, Hashem of Hosts, seated on a high and exalted throne. He said to me: Yishmael My son, bless Me. I said: May it be Your will that Your mercy conquer Your anger… and that You deal with Your children with the attribute of mercy. And He nodded His head to me."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 54a, Beshalach — “Rabbi Abba said: I considered all the praises with which they praised the Holy One, blessed be He, and all began with ‘Then’: ‘Then Solomon said’; ‘Then Joshua spoke’; ‘Then Israel sang.’ Why? All the miracles and mighty deeds done for Israel occur when the light of the Holy Ancient One shines in His crowns, engraved and marked in az—in the alef. The alef pierces the darkness and illumines every side. When the alef's illumination joins and reaches the zayin—what is the zayin? 'Hashem's sword is filled with blood'—then He performs miracles and mighty deeds, because alef has joined with zayin. This is song, song on every side; this is 'Then Moshe sang.'” The Zohar reads az, 'then,' through its letters, alef and zayin. Rav Tzadok applies the same joining of supernal illumination with the lower levels to the future 'Then our mouth shall be filled with laughter.'

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 224a (Ra'aya Meheimna, Pinchas) — "Shemirah is certainly in the heart… therefore 'Shamor' is in the heart and not in any other place; and remembrance (zechirah) is in the male, in the brain that rides upon and rules the heart, and there is no remembrance except in the brain. Therefore 'Zachor' is for the male and 'Shamor' for the female."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 92b (Yisro) — "Zachor — a place that has no forgetting, and forgetting does not exist in it… but below there is forgetting, a place where remembering is needed."

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 65b (Acharei Mos) — "The Yud at first is the totality of all, hidden on every side... The upper tip of the Yud alludes to Ayin (Nothingness)." Zohar III 10b (Vayikra): "The Yud of the holy Name is tied with three knots: one tip above, one below and one in the middle. The tip above is Kesser Elyon, highest of all the highest, head of all heads."
